articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and Issues New FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) on October 16, 2026, issued an amended Venezuela-related General License (GL) and a new Frequently Asked Question (FAQ). This action aims to provide updated guidance and clarify the scope of authorized activities concerning Venezuela sanctions.

The specifics of the amended GL and the new FAQ were not immediately detailed in the announcement, but such updates typically involve adjustments to existing authorizations for certain transactions or operations, or provide interpretive guidance on complex sanctions provisions.

These changes are part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to fine-tune sanctions programs in response to evolving political and economic conditions, ensuring that humanitarian aid and certain legitimate business activities can continue while maintaining pressure on the Venezuelan regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Cuba Entity; Issues New and Amended General Licenses
body: On October 15, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities related to Iran and one entity connected to Cuba. Concurrently, OFAC issued new and amended General Licenses (GLs) along with updated Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to provide guidance on these actions.

The designations are part of the U.S. government's ongoing strategy to counter illicit activities and pressure these regimes. The specific entities designated and the reasons for their inclusion on the sanctions list were not immediately detailed in the public announcement.

The issuance of new and amended GLs and FAQs suggests that OFAC is also working to mitigate unintended consequences of the sanctions, potentially by authorizing certain transactions or clarifying compliance requirements for businesses and individuals.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Entity from Venezuela-Related Designations List
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced on October 14, 2026, the removal of an entity from its Venezuela-related designations list. This action indicates a potential shift in the U.S. government's sanctions strategy concerning Venezuela.

While the specific entity removed was not identified in the initial announcement, such removals often follow a review of the entity's activities, changes in its ownership or control, or a determination that it no longer meets the criteria for designation.

This delisting could signal a willingness by OFAC to adjust sanctions in response to positive developments or to encourage certain behaviors, though the broader Venezuela sanctions program remains in effect.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: On October 13, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities. These actions are part of a broader U.S. government effort to disrupt illicit financial networks globally.

The designations aim to sever financial ties and limit the operational capabilities of those involved in drug trafficking and supporting terrorist organizations. The specific names and details of the designated parties were not immediately released in the public announcement.
These measures underscore the U.S. commitment to combating transnational criminal organizations and terrorist groups by targeting their financial infrastructure and support networks.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced on October 9, 2026, the issuance of a new Russia-related General License (GL). This action provides specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under existing Russia sanctions programs.

General Licenses are often issued to clarify the scope of sanctions, permit humanitarian activities, or allow for the orderly wind-down of certain operations. The details of this new GL were not immediately specified in the announcement.

This move reflects OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, allowing for adjustments to minimize unintended economic impacts while maintaining pressure on the Russian government in response to its actions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Amends Russia-Related General License
body: On October 8, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities related to Iran. Concurrently, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License (GL) and an amended Russia-related GL.

The Iran-related designations are part of ongoing efforts to counter the Iranian regime's destabilizing activities. The new Iran-related GL likely provides specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited.

The amendment to the Russia-related GL indicates a continuous adjustment of sanctions policy to address evolving circumstances and ensure clarity for compliance. The precise details of these designations and GLs were not immediately available.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Designations Removals, Updates, and Iran-Related Alert
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced on October 5, 2026, several designations removals and updates, alongside the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ). These actions reflect ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy.

The removals and updates to designations indicate a dynamic approach to sanctions lists, potentially reflecting changes in circumstances of previously sanctioned entities or individuals. The Iran-related OFAC Alert serves to warn the public about specific illicit finance risks or evasion tactics related to Iran.

The amended Iran-related FAQ provides further clarification on existing sanctions, helping businesses and individuals navigate compliance requirements. These measures collectively aim to enhance the effectiveness of sanctions while providing necessary guidance.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: On October 2, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter terrorism activities. This action is part of the U.S. government's continuous efforts to combat global terrorism and disrupt its financial networks.

These designations aim to isolate those who provide material support to terrorist organizations, preventing them from accessing the U.S. financial system. The specific details of the designated parties were not immediately disclosed in the public announcement.
The imposition of these sanctions underscores the U.S. commitment to protecting national security by targeting the financial infrastructure that enables terrorist operations worldwide.

articles.headline: Bank of America Fined $11,662,930 in OFAC Settlement for Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to a settlement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) totaling $11,662,930. This penalty addresses apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs, including those related to Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

The settlement is part of a broader coordinated enforcement action by the U.S. Treasury, which also saw FinCEN assess a $1.2 billion penalty and the OCC impose a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America for Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) failures.

OFAC's settlement specifically addresses 475 apparent sanctions violations. This action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to enforcing sanctions regulations and holding financial institutions accountable for compliance failures.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Settles with OFAC for $175,015
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics has reached a settlement agreement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), agreeing to pay $175,015. This settlement addresses apparent violations of OFAC sanctions regulations.

The details of the specific violations committed by Pegasus Worldwide Logistics were not immediately disclosed in the public announcement. OFAC settlements typically involve companies that have engaged in transactions or activities prohibited by U.S. sanctions programs.

This enforcement action highlights OFAC's continued efforts to ensure compliance with U.S. sanctions laws across various industries, including logistics and shipping, to prevent illicit financial flows and support national security objectives.

articles.headline: Individual Fined $1,427,230 by OFAC
body: An individual has been assessed a civil penalty of $1,427,230 by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This enforcement action addresses violations of U.S. sanctions regulations.

The specific details of the individual's violations were not immediately released. OFAC frequently takes enforcement actions against individuals who engage in transactions or activities prohibited by various sanctions programs, often involving dealings with sanctioned countries or entities.

This penalty serves as a reminder of OFAC's authority to pursue enforcement actions against individuals, as well as corporations, for non-compliance with sanctions laws, underscoring the importance of individual accountability.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
